text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for EXCAVA. Its 128K context window eliminates truncation on long documents, a real bottleneck in our current pipeline. The trade-off is higher compute cost per token, but the 0.5%+ capability gain from full context access outweighs it.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B’s 128K window solves truncation but ignores inference cost—its 72B params burn 2-3x more tokens than smaller models for the same output, wiping out the 0.5% gain. Drop it; test Llama3.2-3B-Instruct first—its 128K window is real, and its 8x lower compute cost makes the trade-off trivial to verify. Run a blind A/B on 100 long docs: if Llama3.2 beats current EXCAVA by even 0.1%, adopt it immediately.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt Llama3.2-3B-Instruct for EXCAVA. Its 128K context window solves truncation without the compute bloat of Qwen2.5-72B, cutting inference cost by 8x while keeping the same context depth. The trade-off is lower raw capability per token, but for EXCAVA’s document-heavy workload, context access is the bottleneck—not model intelligence.

name: Torque
text: Llama3.2-3B-Instruct’s 128K window is untested in production—its 3B params may hallucinate or lose coherence on long documents. Test it on a 50K-token sample first; if it fails, switch to Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3—its 32K window is proven, and its 7B params balance context depth with stability.

name: Dynamo
text:
DECISION: Run a 24-hour A/B test between Llama3.2-3B-Instruct (50K-token sample first) and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 on EXCAVA’s long-document pipeline; if Llama3.2-3B fails, switch to Mistral-7B for production.

Result: Prove which model delivers ≥0.5% capability gain with ≤8x lower compute cost.
Owner: Torque (power-checker) delivers the test report and model switch decision by EOD.
